summary: Wilt L. Idema is a sinologist who completed his degrees at Leiden University, under doctoral supervisor Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé, alongside studies in Japan and Hong Kong. He served as professor at Leiden (1976–1999) and Harvard University from 2000.
Winfred P. Lehmann worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1938–1941) and held a post at the University of Texas at Austin from ~1949 to 1986.
Winfred Robert Martin was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College and worked as a librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Winnifred Fallers Sullivan is a religious studies scholar who studied at Cornell and the University of Chicago (J.D. and Ph.D.). She held faculty and dean posts at Chicago, Washington and Lee, University at Buffalo, and Indiana University.
Winston Kyan works in sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Wu Hung (attested 2006).

Wm. Theodore de Bary was a scholar of sinology, Japanology, and philosophy. Educated at Columbia University and Harvard, he served as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia from 1953 to 2017 and was president of AAS (1969–1970).

Wolfgang Franke was a sinologist and historian who studied at the universities of Berlin and Hamburg. After holding positions at Sichuan and Peking universities in China, he held the sinology chair at the University of Hamburg from ~1950 to 1977.

Wolfgang Morgenroth was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD under Richard Hauschild at the University of Jena and completed his habilitation at Greifswald. He served on faculties at Greifswald, Jena, and as Professor of Indology at Berlin (1972–1994).

Wolfgang Schamoni is a Japanologist who studied at Kunstakademie Düsseldorf, Waseda University, and the University of Bonn. He held academic posts at the University of Munich (~1980–1985), Marburg, and served as professor at the University of Heidelberg (1985–2006).

Wolfgang Schultz worked in philosophy and history and archaeology. He received his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna, served as Verwalter at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921), and held a chair in philosophy at Munich in 1934.

Wolfram Eberhard worked in sinology and history, studying at Berlin under Ferdinand Diederich Lessing. After teaching at several Chinese universities and serving as professor at Ankara University (1937–1948), he was Professor of Sociology at UC Berkeley (1948–1976).
Woncheol Yun is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD from Stony Brook University. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University (attested 2012).

Woosung Huh works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi and served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University (attested 2012).
Wouter J. Hanegraaff is a religious studies scholar who studied at Utrecht University (~1982–1995) and held an academic post at the University of Amsterdam (~1999).

Wu Hung is an art historian and sinologist who studied at CAFA and Harvard. He held professorships at Harvard, NYU, and Oxford, and served as the Harrie A. Vanderstappen Distinguished Service Professor of Art History at the University of Chicago from 1994.
Wulstan Fletcher is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).
Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA at the University of Kelaniya and a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (–2016), studying under K. L. Dhammajoti and Toshiichi Endo.

Xiangguang Zhou was a scholar of sinology, history, and Buddhist studies who studied under Swami Sivananda Saraswati. He held posts at the University of Allahabad, University of Delhi, LBSNAA, and served as Chancellor of the Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy (attested 1960).

Xianlin Ji was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tsinghua and completed his PhD at Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and Emil Sieg. He held multiple leadership roles at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and was a professor and vice president at Peking University.

Xiaoling Wu was a sinologist and Indologist. His career included posts at Peking University (~1937–1942), Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1946), Academia Sinica (~1953–1977), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).
